script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Monday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed three point seven nine percent down on the session. Semiconductors took a broad hit, and the reasons behind that selloff are worth unpacking carefully.

A state-backed Chinese company began mass producing chip-making machines on Monday, and that single headline was enough to send the entire semiconductor complex into a sharp, disorderly retreat before the opening bell had even settled.

The Nasdaq pulled back meaningfully on Monday as semiconductor stocks led the broader market lower, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF dropping three point seven percent on the session. Geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran eased over the weekend, sending crude oil prices sharply lower — but that relief provided no cushion for chip names, which faced dual headwinds from China.

Two developments out of China defined Monday's session for this portfolio. First, reports confirmed that a state-backed Chinese firm has begun mass producing chip-making equipment — a direct competitive threat to the equipment manufacturers represented heavily here. Second, ChangXin Memory Technologies, known as CXMT, delivered a blockbuster debut on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, rattling memory chip investors globally. CXMT's IPO raised the competitive stakes for memory leaders like Micron Technology, with analysts at Insider Monkey noting the event pressured memory and storage names broadly. Together, these two catalysts created a pincer movement on the semiconductor space — equipment names sold off on the manufacturing threat, memory names sold off on the IPO signal, and the damage spread across the entire sector with little discrimination.

Advanced Micro Devices was down five point one seven percent on Monday's session. The selloff tracked the broader chip weakness tied to the China equipment news, and separately, reports emerged that Nvidia is in talks to finance OpenAI — a development that carries competitive implications for Advanced Micro Devices in the data center artificial intelligence market. Watch for any further detail on that financing arrangement as the week develops.

Micron Technology was down two point two five percent on the session. The CXMT IPO was the direct catalyst here — memory-chip stocks Micron and SK Hynix both fell as the Chinese rival's debut signaled intensifying competition in the global memory market. Despite Monday's pressure, a longer-range analyst note suggested Micron's stock could appreciate significantly by late two thousand twenty-seven, calling the current level a buying opportunity. The next major test will be any management commentary on pricing and supply dynamics.

Nvidia was down four point nine nine percent on the session. Nvidia announced an investment in Ilya Sutskever's artificial intelligence startup Safe Superintelligence, supplying Vera Rubin systems — a signal of continued deep engagement in frontier AI infrastructure. The OpenAI financing report added a separate dimension. Nvidia has underperformed the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index significantly this year, up just five point four percent versus the index's sixty-three percent gain.

Broadcom was down two point three six percent on the session. Analyst commentary published Monday framed the question for investors as a direct comparison between Broadcom and Nvidia for AI capital expenditure exposure — noting that Broadcom's model captures a different segment of the buildout. The stock remains more than twenty percent below its recent high. The upcoming earnings cycle will be the key test.

Intel was down zero point seven zero percent on the session — the most resilient name in the portfolio on Monday, suggesting relative defensive positioning or simply less direct exposure to the China equipment and memory catalysts that hit peers harder.

Turning to Applied Materials — down eight point one six percent on the session, the sharpest single-name loss in the portfolio Monday. The report of a state-backed Chinese firm mass producing chip-making equipment struck directly at Applied Materials' core competitive positioning. This is the most significant single-stock damage from Monday's session and warrants close attention to any analyst revisions this week.

KLA Corporation was down three point four zero percent on the session. As a semiconductor equipment and process control name, KLA faces the same China production threat as Applied Materials, though Monday's move was comparatively more contained.

Over at Marvell Technology — down two point six one percent on the session. Marvell carries significant exposure to custom artificial intelligence silicon for hyperscalers, and the broad chip retreat pulled it lower. Upcoming hyperscaler earnings will be a direct read on Marvell's demand pipeline.

Lam Research was down four point four six percent on the session. Another equipment name, Lam Research absorbed meaningful losses tied to the China chip-making machine reports — the same fundamental threat that hit Applied Materials and KLA.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was down three point nine seven percent on the session. As the world's leading contract chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor sits at the intersection of every major theme in play Monday — China competition, AI demand cycles, and geopolitical positioning. It remains a bellwether for the entire portfolio.

Three data points to track in the next forty-eight hours. First, the Federal Open Market Committee meeting — any language shift on rate trajectory directly affects technology sector valuations. Second, earnings reports from major hyperscalers including Microsoft and Meta, expected mid-week, which will provide direct signal on artificial intelligence capital expenditure commitments. Third, any further detail on the Chinese chip-making equipment program and whether U.S. export control authorities respond formally.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the hyperscaler earnings closely — they will set the tone for every name in this portfolio for the remainder of the week.
